basis: Complement-mediated microangiopathy defined by hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury; extrarenal cardiac and CNS injury are minority manifestations.
Callosal dysgenesis and spasms establish CNS involvement; the unspecified cleft does not establish another organ axis.
Choriocarcinoma originating in the central nervous system.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by intellectual disability and movement abnormalities, both reported in 80-99%.
Intellectual disability defines the disease; hearing impairment and bilateral ptosis each occur in 1/3 reported patients. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
Cortical and callosal malformations with seizures and developmental impairment; nystagmus is occasional and does not establish ocular damage.
Heart defects, developmental impairment and digital anomalies define the syndrome; hearing loss occurs in 26/49. Eyelid abnormalities, including ptosis in 23/49, omitted because of cap.
Peroxisomal disease commonly causes developmental impairment, retinal dystrophy and sensorineural hearing loss (each typically >30%); hepatic dysfunction omitted because of cap.
Ovarian epithelial neoplasm; reproductive origin has no axis. Mucinous morphology does not establish gastrointestinal disease.
Neurodevelopmental and movement disorder with defining persistent oculomotor abnormalities. Reflux is separately diagnosed; feeding symptoms do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
T. cruzi infection directly causes myocarditis and cardiomyopathy in about 30%; digestive injury is under 30%. Organ enlargement and transient rash alone do not establish damage.
Severe intellectual disability and delayed sexual maturation define the reported syndrome; proportionate short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Otosclerosis causes progressive conductive or sensorineural hearing loss; localized otic bone remodeling belongs to the ear axis.
Inherited childhood-onset dystonia, documented in both reported patients; muscle contractions arise from neurologic dysfunction.
Mitochondrial disorder defined by neuropathy, ataxia and retinal degeneration; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Neurogenic weakness alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Respiratory-chain disease with neurodegeneration, neuropathy and structural mitochondrial myopathy. Respiratory insufficiency from muscle weakness does not establish direct lung damage.
Acute inflammatory injury of renal tubules and interstitium, usually mediated by an immune hypersensitivity response.
Severe Zellweger disease commonly causes brain malformations, hepatic dysfunction and renal cystic disease (each about >30%); hearing and retinal disease omitted because of cap.
Benign neoplasm occupying the central nervous system; endocrine involvement applies only to selected subtypes.
Primary endometrial carcinoma has reproductive origin; resemblance to urothelial cells does not establish urinary tract involvement.
Reactive glandular metaplasia and cystic inflammation of the bladder; no specific infectious or autoimmune mechanism is established.
Leukopenia and abnormal neutrophils with recurrent bacterial and viral infections establish a blood-cell disorder with immunodeficiency.
Inherited atrial cardiac rhythm disorder; thromboembolic complications are risks rather than additional defining organ damage.
GRM1-related cerebellar neurodegeneration; persistent esotropia occurs in 30-79% and ptosis in 3/10. A neurotransmitter receptor defect alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Carcinoma originating in the epithelial cells of the gastric cardia.
